page: Amazon Web Services m6id.16xlarge is a general-purpose, 6th-generation instance designed to balance multi-threaded compute, system memory, and direct-attached storage. Built on the AWS Nitro System, the instance features an Intel Xeon Platinum 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. It provides 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, accompanied by 54 MB of L3 cache, 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, and a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps. The architecture includes hardware support for AVX-512 extensions and cryptographic instructions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

A major defining element of the m6id.16xlarge is its bundled 3,800 GB NVMe SSD instance storage. This local block capacity delivers low-latency, high-throughput IO directly attached to the host, avoiding network storage hops. Synthetic benchmarks reflect solid data throughput, with passmark database operations reaching 26,484.23 and static web serving throughput attaining 45.66 GB/sec, placing both in the top 25% tier. Redis SET operations perform at an average mark of 54.74 million operations per second.

The CPU profile delivers strong aggregate throughput across multi-core workloads, supported by a passmark CPU score of 57,701.18 and a stress-ng multi-core benchmark of 61,949.91. Computational strengths also emerge in parallel tasks such as Clang software compilation and ray tracing. Conversely, single-thread performance is balanced within the middle 50% tier, as demonstrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,697.0 and stress-ng single-core result of 1,894.0. Without dedicated GPU acceleration, large-scale LLM inference is limited on 70B parameter models, producing 3.13 tokens per second for generation, while smaller 135M parameter models achieve 267.82 tokens per second.

The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio paired with extensive local NVMe SSD capacity makes the m6id.16xlarge cost-efficient for heavy I/O operations and medium-scale caching without incurring supplementary network storage charges. It is directly suited for relational and key-value database clusters, large CI/CD build farms, transactional web serving, and continuous ETL workloads requiring swift local temporary scratch space.
description: Amazon Web Services m6id.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 64 vCPUs (32 physical cores) powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor at 3.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR4 RAM, 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and 3,800 GB of bundled NVMe SSD local storage, it offers a balanced 1:4 CPU-to-memory configuration alongside fast physical disk access. Benchmark results indicate top-quartile multi-core CPU metrics, software compilation speed, and static web serving throughput reaching 45.66 GB/sec, while single-core metrics fall into the average range. Lacking hardware GPU accelerators, it focuses strictly on CPU-bound and I/O-intensive workloads. The m6id.16xlarge is best fit for high-throughput databases, temporary cache nodes, CI/CD pipeline compilation, and transactional web backend systems.
